page-1: Runspindle Refinery A human-guided evaluation loop Runspindle contributors Adapted from SRC-013; copyright 2026 newdarwindev November 2026 | Reviewed design adaptation Abstract An opt-in refinement layer can turn selected agent-assisted workflows into versioned candidates for evaluation. An accountable owner defines the task and data permissions; reviewers minimize examples and curate a golden dataset; bounded experiments compare a baseline with DSPy program configurations or eligible smaller models. Exact candidate evidence, separate release approval and a verified rollback path precede serving. This paper states a testable design, not a deployed system, a measured improvement or permission to collect data. All diagram labels are synthetic. Evidence boundary. This is a new compilation of an adapted paper, not the historical PDF and not a runtime acceptance result. Component tests, historical demonstrations, provider-backed experiments and live acceptance are different evidence classes. The repository’s versioned implementation evidence remains authoritative for what has actually run. 1 Thesis and boundary Repeated computational patterns may justify a narrower, maintained workflow. That is a conditional research thesis: human judgment, relationships, physical work, legal obligations and consent remain important limits. Repetition does not authorize a schedule, collection of conversations, provider transmission or new account access. A portfolio of bounded programs and models can be coordinated under human governance. The useful unit is a workflow revision: stable inputs, permitted effects, target bindings, exception policy, acceptance criteria and resource budget. A successful completion or an attractive prompt is not that contract. Optimizing a candidate must not change authority, credentials, tool grants or deployment configuration. Execution and learning are separate. A human correction is first an execution event. It becomes an example only after separate consent, minimization, provenance and suitability review. A feedback signal is not release approval, and release approval does not authorize new effects. 1
page-2: 2 A controlled refinement loop 1. Select and authorize. Record the owner, task revision, approved sources and destinations, output contract, exclusions and stop conditions. Collection and external-provider use need their own scope. Nothing is captured by default. 2. Review and redact. Inspect proposed examples before admission. Remove secrets, identifiers and unrelated material. Bind feedback to exact source and output revisions, content hashes and its intended target. Quarantine incomplete, conflicting, stale or non-replayable evidence rather than trusting an eligibility flag. 3. Curate and lock. Version dataset bytes, labeling rules, adjudications, exclusions and split manifest. Keep related thread, run and revision families in one partition; deduplicate before splitting. Lock held-out cases before optimization. Do not select candidates on repeated held- out feedback or silently replace a failed split. 4. Choose bounded candidates. Pin baseline and candidate bytes, DSPy version, model and provider configuration, metric implementation, optimizer and thresholds. Restrict optimization to training data. Reserve one cumulative call, token, time and cost budget across search, re- flection, scoring, baseline/candidate evaluation and retries. Record cancellation or exhaustion; unknown usage cannot be counted as zero. 5. Evaluate. Compare baseline and candidate on the same locked cases. Include refusal, human exceptions, uncertain effects and out-of-scope requests. Report attempted, usable and excluded counts, error categories, quality, safety, latency, intervention burden and total measured cost. Unknown safety or cost blocks a pass. Byte equality in a synthetic fixture is not general model- quality evidence. 6. Approve and promote. Authenticate the approver independently. Bind the decision to artifact bytes and digest, evaluation evidence, thresholds and target serving scope. A Boolean or actor label is not authority. Use durable atomic updates, concurrency control and append-only audit evidence. A registry update is not proof that a serving process loaded the candidate. 7. Observe and roll back. Verify the loaded digest, permitted task boundary and defined metrics. A failed load keeps the last approved version active. Rollback identifies a compatible, available, previously approved artifact, retains output attribution and records the reason. Reconcile an uncertain result before retrying. 2
page-3: 3 Testable hypotheses H1: narrower candidates. Some bounded workflows may run on smaller models at acceptable qual- ity. Compare baseline and candidate with a fixed task, held-out cases and complete cost accounting. Count failed attempts and human repair; zero accepted completions has no finite cost-per-accepted- task result. H2: reviewed data. Human-adjudicated golden datasets may improve repeatability and error dis- covery. Compare agreement, coverage and recurring failures across declared dataset versions without contaminating evaluation. H3: governed release. Versioned artifacts, scoped approvals and rollback may improve repro- ducibility and recovery. Test reviewability, unauthorized promotion, altered bytes, concurrent writes and failed-load recovery in controlled trials. No experiment result, score, savings estimate or benchmark is asserted. Historical simulated interface scores are excluded from this adaptation. 4 Research domains and limits Possible domains include internal routing, support triage, summary or document work, and separately permissioned research into opportunities. Each needs domain-specific evaluation, appropriate data rights and organizational controls. This paper authorizes no applications, bids, outreach, submissions, purchases or deployment. A possible autonomous operating mode remains bounded by human gates and the applicable policy. Quality gains are not guaranteed. Dataset bias, incomplete feedback, distribution shift, annotation disagreement and optimization overfitting can defeat apparently strong results. Integration, evalu- ation, maintenance and recovery costs may outweigh savings at low volume. Changes to models or platforms require renewed comparisons. Safe failures and authority violations cannot be traded against a higher aggregate score. 5 Prototype scope and evidence The selected historical artifact described a synthetic interactive showcase of selection, review, simulated evaluation, promotion and rollback. It did not establish a deployed DSPy service. Its historical UI tests and walkthrough are not rerun or imported here; unselected application code and operational records are outside this lift. This adaptation aligns that argument with the current Runspindle experiment and desired-intent contracts. It does not replace component evidence, certify current deployment, or assert that every specified control is implemented. Local scripted or disposable synthetic tests cannot establish real- provider quality, trusted live collection or production readiness. See the versioned implementation evidence and status record for narrower claims and remaining gaps. 3
page-4: 6 Eight architecture views The following eight reviewed vector diagrams preserve the selected source’s conceptual mechanisms. They contain invented labels, not operational snapshots. Their original color convention is retained: solid teal describes a conceptual binding or explicit scenario premise; dashed amber marks a proposed path. Neither color proves that a Runspindle service exists or has passed acceptance. The diagrams are retained historical assets embedded in a newly compiled adaptation. Surrounding text supplies current constraints; historical terminology such as GitOps, always-on hosts or cluster choices is illustrative, not a deployment requirement or report about the owner’s infrastructure. 6.1 Durable identity binding A verified route links repository/worktree, selected host, process, native managed session and desti- nation. Names alone are not authority. Preserve explicit host pins, lease epochs and exact task/intent revisions in the relevant runtime contract. Attribution does not require transcript collection. Repository canonical match Host bind Managed session attribute Channel + thread bounded worktree process identity durable context veriﬁed route Unique worktree + owner + process checks No transcript needed for identity Figure 1. Verified identity supports attribution; it does not grant collection or execution permission. 6.2 Managed-session lifecycle Owner-gated admission precedes launch; verified session-start evidence precedes binding. External sessions remain observation-only unless separately enrolled. Resume, interruption and stop must use the bound identity and current authority. Lost or uncertain control results need reconciliation before retry. Owner-gated Veriﬁed Managed turn Stopped or Idle completed launch session bind active Interrupt / resume / stop require bound identity External session no control grant observe only Figure 2. Observing a session and controlling it are distinct scopes. 4
page-5: 6.3 Reaction, approval and execution A reaction or request is evidence to inspect in its authorized context, not a universal grant. Verify actor, target, intended action, limits and timing. Existing scoped approval can cover a particular step; feedback classification cannot expand it. Verify the outcome before advancing or retrying. Reaction or Verify actor Resolve scope Reviewable Execute only request signal and context and authority action plan authorized step A reaction is evidence, not permission Actor, target, limits, and timing Verify result; reconcile uncertainty Figure 3. Evidence, policy evaluation, approval and effect execution remain separate. 6.4 Reviewed golden-data provenance Every admitted example retains source/output versions, feedback target, consent and review dispo- sition. Stable family IDs and deduplication precede the locked train/validation/held-out partition. The historical diagram’s deterministic privacy and leakage gates are necessary pipeline checks, not model-quality scores. Invented / approved Human review Stable group IDs Versioned examples and redaction deduplicate split Train Validate Held out Oﬄine format / privacy / leakage gates; no quality claim Figure 4. Related examples remain together; held-out data never guides optimization. 5
page-6: 6.5 Experiment and deployment control planes The experiment plane produces evidence within a fixed budget; it cannot approve its own release. A separate release path checks exact bytes, digest, thresholds, target scope and authenticated approval. The historical Git-reviewed/GitOps path illustrates separation of duties, not an implemented deploy- ment mechanism. A serving-load acknowledgement must be distinguished from a registry commit. Experiment plane (proposed) Scoped experiment Isolated evaluation Versioned result request job + evidence GitOps Reviewed Git Human approval reconciliation reference of exact version Deployment plane (proposed); never the experiment runner Figure 5. A good score is not deployment authority. 6.6 Manually placed compute constellation This retained figure is an explicitly hypothetical development scenario: a human chooses app-to-host placement and host availability is assumed. Compose and a single cluster are historical examples, not recommendations or requirements for current infrastructure. No uptime, cluster, machine identity or deployment claim follows. Refinery remains a separately authorized layer. Human operator manual placement Always-on host A Always-on host B Always-on host C selected app selected app selected app Reﬁnery candidate Dev choice: Compose ﬁrst; one K3s cluster optional separate future layer Figure 6. Placement and availability assumptions must be made explicit before operational evaluation. 6
page-7: 6.7 Versioned provenance chain An approved source becomes a reviewed dataset version, then a bounded experiment’s candidate and a separately approved promotion record. Preserve exact source/output feedback lineage, locked split/metric/configuration versions, artifact bytes and digest, release evidence and rollback pointer. A graph edge is a required evidence link, not proof of a live training pipeline. Approved Review + Dataset Candidate Promotion source redaction version artifact record Grouped splits + held-out evidence Approval + rollback pointer Figure 7. Each stage retains the evidence and authority for that specific transition. 6.8 Observation versus failure Observation freshness decreases with time. A missing update is unknown, not proof of failure or permission to restart. Require a verified process/session check and current action authority before control. Preserve stale, failed and uncertain states distinctly so automation does not turn incomplete telemetry into an external effect. Veriﬁed process check before control observed activity age increases unknown, not failure time start observation no update check Figure 8. Fresh, aging and unknown describe observations, not automatic control decisions. 7
